newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Bancos de Venezuela, Consolidado base prices set.
newsitem.headline: Bancos de Venezuela, Consolidado base prices set.

text.p: The base prices for Venezuelan banks Banco de Venezuela and Banco Consolidado have been set at $366 million and $148 million respectively for their auctions on December 19, Venezuelan state deposits guarantee fund Fogade said.

The base price for Colombian bank Banco Tequendama, currently 99 percent held by Fogade, has also been set at $48 million and will be auctioned December 20, Fogade President Esther de Margulis told reporters.
Margulis said the Banco de Venezuela price included $80 million in non-financial assets, including the Custravalca security company, which would be sold separately.
"Speaking strictly of share value, Banco de Venzuela's price has been set at $286 million," Margulis said.

In August, a proposed Banco de Venezuela sale was cancelled after investors were scared away by supposed irregularities in the auction process. At that time, Fogade had set Banco de Venezuela's base price at $275 million.
With 20 percent of Banco de Venezuela and Consolidado shares due to be sold to small Venezuelan investors, "We really hope that this time we obtain a good premium on the base prices," Margulis said.
Margulis added a further $15 million in suspended dividend payments may have to be added to Consolidado's $148 million base price. Trade in Banco Consolidado shares was halted in May 1994.
Fogade's legal counsel added that claims on the banks lodged by fugitive financier Alvaro Stelling, former owner of Banco de Venezuela and Consolidado, were without foundation.
